name_note: The species was published as Eubacterium biforme and some genomes GTDB assigns here are still deposited in NCBI under older names.

sentences.text: Holdemanella biformis is a gut bacterium of the family Erysipelotrichaceae whose name was created by reclassifying Eubacterium biforme.
A strain of Holdemanella biformis was isolated from the feces of a metabolically healthy human volunteer.
In culture Holdemanella biformis produced a high concentration of the long chain fatty acid C18-3OH, which was shown to be an agonist of peroxisome proliferator activated receptor gamma.
A study identified Holdemanella biformis as the human counterpart of the murine Faecalibaculum rodentium and reported both strongly under-represented during tumourigenesis.
A study reported that Holdemanella biformis ameliorated hyperglycemia, improved oral glucose tolerance and restored insulin signaling in the liver of obese mice.
